settings.title: When Indoor Air Becomes a Concern

settings.editor:
Many homes have air quality issues that go unnoticed. Germs, allergens, and mold can spread through your HVAC system and impact the health of everyone indoors. Here are signs that it may be time to consider a solution like germicidal lights:

  • Frequent allergy or asthma flare-ups
  • Musty odors near vents or inside living spaces
  • Mold growth in damp areas
  • Illnesses that seem to linger or return

Indoor air quality affects your health, and germicidal lights are a smart way to improve it. We’ll install and service your system so it’s working effectively from day one. With decades of experience and a dedication to reliable service, our team has been here since 1984 to help you breathe easier. Here’s why our customers trust us:

  • Transparent pricing with no surprise costs
  • Our “Done Right” guarantee on every service
  • Courteous technicians who keep your home clean
  • A local company committed to serving our neighbors

Upgrading your home with germicidal lights is an investment in long-term health and comfort. That’s why we offer financing options through GoodLeap, Synchrony and Hearth. These plans make it easier to move forward now instead of putting it off. We’ll walk you through the choices so you can pick what works best for your household.

Our technicians install germicidal UV lights inside your HVAC system, where air passes before circulating through your home. These lights target mold spores, bacteria, and viruses, breaking them down at the source. We’ll carefully place and set up the system for maximum effectiveness without impacting your system’s performance. If you already have UV lights, we also service and replace bulbs to keep them working at full strength. With proper installation and maintenance, you’ll have cleaner air moving throughout your entire home all the time.

Ignoring your indoor air quality problems can affect more than comfort. Without treatment, airborne contaminants continue to spread every time your HVAC system runs. This can create long-term health issues and strain your system. Here are some possible risks:

  • Increased allergies and respiratory symptoms
  • Persistent mold growth inside ducts and coils
  • Lower system efficiency from excessive buildup
  • Higher medical costs due to ongoing illness

Installing germicidal lights offers lasting improvements for your home and your health. These systems work silently in the background, treating your indoor air around the clock. You’ll notice fresher air and a cleaner living environment, along with fewer worries about hidden contaminants. Benefits include:

  • Reduced bacteria, mold, and viruses in circulated air
  • Fresher-smelling indoor spaces without chemical sprays
  • Improved HVAC performance with less buildup on coils
  • Healthier living conditions for the whole family

items.item_title: How do germicidal lights work in HVAC systems?
Are germicidal lights safe for my home?
How often do germicidal lights need maintenance?
Can germicidal lights help with allergies?
Do germicidal lights eliminate all indoor air problems?
Will UV lights affect my HVAC system?
Can I install germicidal lights myself?

settings.editor: Germicidal lights, often called UV-C lights, are devices that emit ultraviolet light to neutralize bacteria, viruses, and mold spores. They’re typically installed inside HVAC systems, so they treat the air as it circulates. This creates a healthier indoor environment for your home.

These lights are placed near coils or within ducts where they shine on passing air. The UV light damages the DNA of microorganisms, stopping them from multiplying. As a result, germs and mold are neutralized before reaching your living spaces.

Yes, when installed by trained technicians, UV-C lights are completely safe. They’re contained within your HVAC system, so the light doesn’t reach your living space. The only thing you’ll notice is cleaner, fresher air.

Most UV bulbs last about a year before they need to be replaced. We recommend adding the replacement to your routine HVAC maintenance schedule. Regular service keeps the system working at full strength.

Yes, by reducing mold spores and bacteria, germicidal lights can ease symptoms for those with allergies or asthma. Cleaner air makes a noticeable difference in comfort. Many homeowners report fewer flare-ups after installation.

While they’re highly effective against germs and mold, they don’t remove dust, pet dander, or chemical pollutants. For full indoor air quality improvement, they’re often combined with filters or air purifiers. Together, these systems offer complete protection.

Germicidal lights actually help your system by keeping coils cleaner and reducing microbial buildup. This improves airflow and efficiency. Over time, it can also extend the lifespan of your equipment.

Installation should be done by a trained technician because placement and safety are critical for effectiveness. DIY setups can lead to poor performance or even damage to your system. Professional installation guarantees the lights do their job properly.

Most germicidal light installations can be completed in a single visit, often within a couple of hours. The exact time depends on your system’s layout. We’ll let you know what to expect before starting.
